questions.answer: Off campus

questions.answer: It was pretty easy, there is a lot of sites with a lot of houses. Such as oakhouse, Sakuahouse and the one i used BeGoodJapan

questions.answer: For some people there can be some transport time

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In hindsight  te system itself is fine, as you could sign up for courses have a try out week and then do something else if you did not like it. But that was kind of confusing to us in the moment.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student administration

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of them

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask for help

Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.answer: MA

questions.answer: It was pretty easy. But we also only do passed/failed.

questions.answer: Waseda actually grades on attendance and participation

questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
Regional Integration
Comparative Political Economy of the Global South
Development Economics
Chinese Foreign Policy: International Relations and Strategy
Global Political Economy(Politics)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Comparative Political Economy of the Global South, this one was by far the best

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The bureaucracy is annoying but the trip is worth it
Go to smaller cities, people there are more willing to talk
Enjoy it
